symptoms: Payment API returns 500 Internal Server Error
Transactions fail unexpectedly
Payment requests are unsuccessful
diagnostic_checks: Check dependent services and database connectivity
resolution_steps: Identify the exception from application logs
Verify that dependent services are operational
Check recent configuration or deployment changes
Escalate unresolved application errors to the engineering team
escalation_condition: Escalate if payment failures continue after initial checks or affect multiple transactions.

symptoms: Database connection refused
Connection timeout
Connection pool exhausted
Application cannot retrieve records
resolution_steps: Confirm database server availability
Verify hostname, port and credentials
Inspect connection pool utilization
Escalate persistent database failures to the DBA team
escalation_condition: Escalate if the database remains unavailable or connection failures persist.

symptoms: User does not receive OTP
OTP delivery is delayed
SMS delivery fails
resolution_steps: Verify the registered mobile number
Check whether OTP generation was successful
Inspect SMS gateway delivery logs
Escalate repeated delivery failures to the messaging team
escalation_condition: Escalate if OTP generation or delivery continues to fail.

symptoms: Payment requests time out
API response takes too long
Payment gateway does not respond
resolution_steps: Check payment gateway health
Inspect API latency and application logs
Verify network connectivity
Escalate persistent gateway timeouts to the payment engineering team
escalation_condition: Escalate if timeouts continue or multiple payment requests are affected.

symptoms: Application responds slowly
High CPU utilization
Server performance degradation
resolution_steps: Identify resource-intensive processes
Review recent traffic and application changes
Check for abnormal background jobs
Escalate persistent resource issues to the infrastructure team
escalation_condition: Escalate if high CPU utilization persists or affects application availability.

symptoms: Application cannot reach external service
Connection timeout
Network unreachable error
resolution_steps: Verify network connectivity
Check DNS configuration
Inspect firewall and routing rules
Escalate persistent connectivity issues to the network team
escalation_condition: Escalate if connectivity cannot be restored after initial checks.

symptoms: Customer account shows a debit but payment is marked failed
Payment confirmation is missing
Transaction status differs between bank and application
Customer asks whether a failed payment should be retried
User wants to initiate another payment after a failed transaction
Uncertainty about whether the original payment was completed
Concern about charging the customer again
diagnostic_checks: Record the transaction reference and timestamp
Check the payment transaction status in the authorized payment system
Review gateway response and callback logs
Check whether a reversal or refund status is recorded
Verify the final transaction status before attempting another payment
resolution_steps: Do not initiate a duplicate charge while the original transaction is unresolved
Verify the final transaction status using the approved payment system
If status is pending, follow the documented reconciliation process
Escalate mismatched debit and payment statuses to the payment operations team
escalation_condition: Escalate if the debit is confirmed but the transaction status remains failed or unclear after reconciliation checks.

symptoms: Customer reports being charged more than once
Multiple transaction references exist for one purchase
Duplicate payment notifications are received
diagnostic_checks: Collect all transaction references and timestamps
Compare transaction amounts and merchant references
Check whether both transactions are captured or one is only pending
Review retry and payment request logs
resolution_steps: Verify the status of each transaction in the authorized payment system
Do not manually issue a refund without following the approved refund process
Identify whether duplicate requests originated from client retries or gateway processing
Escalate confirmed duplicate captures to payment operations
escalation_condition: Escalate when multiple captures are confirmed or transaction statuses cannot be reconciled.

symptoms: Transaction remains pending for an unusually long time
No final success or failure response is displayed
Merchant system has not received a final payment status
diagnostic_checks: Check transaction reference and creation time
Inspect callback or webhook delivery logs
Check reconciliation status in the authorized payment system
resolution_steps: Verify the transaction's latest status before retrying
Check whether the gateway callback was received and processed
Follow the approved transaction reconciliation procedure
Escalate unresolved pending transactions to payment operations
escalation_condition: Escalate if the transaction remains pending beyond the configured processing window or status cannot be confirmed.

symptoms: API responds with HTTP 401
Requests fail authentication
Previously working API calls are rejected
diagnostic_checks: Verify that the request includes the required authentication header
Check token expiry and validity using the approved authentication process
resolution_steps: Obtain or refresh credentials through the approved process
Verify the authorization header format without exposing secrets
Confirm that the application is using the intended environment and credentials
Escalate persistent authentication failures to the API or identity team
escalation_condition: Escalate if valid credentials still receive 401 responses or authentication service errors are observed.

symptoms: API responds with HTTP 403
Authenticated user cannot access an endpoint
Access is denied for a specific operation
diagnostic_checks: Inspect API gateway or authorization logs
resolution_steps: Confirm the user or service account has the required permission
Request access changes through the approved access-management process
Verify the endpoint and environment being called
Escalate unexpected authorization denials to the API or security team
escalation_condition: Escalate if permissions appear correct but access remains denied, or if an access-policy issue is suspected.

symptoms: API responds with HTTP 404
Requested resource or endpoint cannot be found
An API route that previously worked is unavailable
diagnostic_checks: Verify the request URL and endpoint path
Check HTTP method and API version
Confirm that the requested resource identifier exists
resolution_steps: Correct any invalid path or resource identifier
Use the documented endpoint and supported HTTP method
Confirm the intended API version and environment
Escalate if a valid endpoint is still unavailable
escalation_condition: Escalate if the documented endpoint or existing resource continues to return 404 after validation.

symptoms: API gateway responds with HTTP 502
Upstream service response is unavailable or invalid
Requests fail at the gateway or proxy layer
diagnostic_checks: Check API gateway or reverse proxy health
Review gateway and upstream application logs
Check recent routing, deployment, or configuration changes
resolution_steps: Confirm the upstream service is running and reachable
Review gateway routing and upstream configuration
Correlate gateway errors with upstream service logs
Escalate persistent gateway failures to the platform or API engineering team
escalation_condition: Escalate if the upstream service is healthy but gateway errors continue, or multiple endpoints are affected.

symptoms: Application pages or operations load slowly when accessing records
Database queries take longer than expected
Query latency has increased
diagnostic_checks: Identify the slow query and its execution time
Inspect the query execution plan where access is authorized
Check database load and recent schema or application changes
resolution_steps: Capture the affected query and relevant timing details
Review the execution plan with the DBA team
Check whether appropriate indexes and query patterns are being used
Escalate persistent query performance issues to database administration
escalation_condition: Escalate if query latency remains high or affects critical application operations.

symptoms: Application reports no available database connections
Requests wait for a database connection or fail
Connection pool utilization remains at its limit
diagnostic_checks: Check current and maximum pool utilization
Inspect application logs for unclosed or long-running connections
Check database connection limits and active sessions
resolution_steps: Identify services or operations holding connections for too long
Review connection lifecycle and ensure connections are released correctly
Compare configured pool limits with database limits
Escalate persistent exhaustion to application engineering and the DBA team
escalation_team: Application Engineering and Database Administration Teams
escalation_condition: Escalate if the pool remains exhausted after initial checks or increasing demand affects application availability.

symptoms: User cannot log in with expected credentials
Login requests are rejected
Authentication errors appear during sign-in
diagnostic_checks: Confirm the user is using the correct account identifier
Review authentication logs for the failure reason
Check whether the account is locked or disabled
resolution_steps: Guide the user through the approved password-reset process if credentials are incorrect
Verify account status through the authorized support process
Check identity service health
Escalate repeated failures affecting multiple users to the identity team
escalation_condition: Escalate if the account is active and credentials are valid but authentication continues to fail, or multiple users are affected.

symptoms: User receives an account locked message
Login is blocked after repeated failed attempts
Authentication fails even when the user believes the password is correct
diagnostic_checks: Verify the account status using the approved support console
Determine whether repeated attempts are coming from a known device or service
resolution_steps: Follow the approved identity-verification procedure
Use the authorized account-unlock process if permitted
Guide the user to reset credentials if required by policy
Escalate suspected unauthorized activity to the security team
escalation_condition: Escalate if the account repeatedly locks after being unlocked or suspicious login activity is detected.

symptoms: Disk utilization approaches its configured threshold
Application logs or files cannot be written
Services report insufficient disk space
resolution_steps: Identify the source of disk growth
Follow approved log-retention and cleanup procedures
Do not delete application or system files without authorization
Escalate if additional capacity or storage maintenance is required
escalation_condition: Escalate if disk utilization reaches the critical threshold, services are affected, or safe cleanup is insufficient.

symptoms: Application service restarts without a planned deployment
Users experience brief service interruptions
Service uptime or process monitoring shows repeated restarts
diagnostic_checks: Check service and system event logs around the restart time
Review process exit codes and crash reports
Review recent deployments, configuration changes, and infrastructure events
resolution_steps: Correlate restart times with logs and monitoring alerts
Identify whether the restart was caused by a crash, resource limit, or planned operation
Follow the approved service recovery procedure
Escalate recurring unexplained restarts to the application or infrastructure engineering team
escalation_condition: Escalate if restarts repeat, cause service disruption, or the root cause cannot be identified.

symptoms: Hostname cannot be resolved
Application cannot connect using a service hostname
DNS lookup returns an error or times out
diagnostic_checks: Check DNS lookup results for the affected hostname
Compare hostname resolution from an affected and an unaffected environment where permitted
Review DNS and network monitoring alerts
resolution_steps: Confirm the hostname is correct
Verify the configured DNS resolver and network reachability
Check the relevant DNS record through the authorized DNS management process
Escalate persistent resolution failures to the network team
escalation_condition: Escalate if valid hostnames continue to fail resolution or multiple services are affected.
